ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, the rectangle $OABC$ has two adjacent sides on the coordinate axes, with vertex $B(6, 4)$. A line passing through point $P(4, m)$ on side $BC$ bisects the area of the rectangle. What is the equation of this line?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} 

Since the adjacent sides of rectangle OABC are on the coordinate axes, and the vertex B is at (6, 4),\\
therefore, the intersection point of the diagonal lines of the rectangle is at (3, 2),\\
since point P(4, m) is a point on side BC,\\
therefore, P(4, 4),\\
since a line passing through the intersection point of the diagonal lines bisects the rectangle,\\
therefore, let the line passing through P(4, m) and bisecting the rectangle be $y=kx+b$,\\
substituting points (4, 4) and (3, 2) yields $\begin{cases}4k+b=4\\ 3k+b=2\end{cases}$,\\
solving, we get $\begin{cases}k=2\\ b=-4\end{cases}$,\\
therefore, the equation of this line is $y=2x-4$.\\
Hence, the answer is: $\boxed{y=2x-4}$.

推理：因为 B=(6,4)，矩形区域为 [0,6]×[0,4]，总面积为 6×4=24。点 P(4,m) 在上边 BC 上，而 BC 的纵坐标为 4，所以 m=4，P=(4,4)。设过 P 的直线为 y-4=k(x-4)。按面积平分要求，直线在矩形内切出的两部分面积都应为 12。对于能满足面积平分的正斜率情形，直线从 P 向左下方与底边 y=0 相交。令 0-4=k(x-4)，得交点横坐标 x=4-4/k。此时直线上方的面积由左侧宽 4-4/k、高 4 的矩形部分和右侧一个三角形组成，面积为 4(4-4/k)+1/2·(4/k)·4=16-16/k+8/k=16-8/k。令其等于矩形面积的一半 12，得 16-8/k=12，所以 8/k=4，k=2。因此直线为 y-4=2(x-4)，即 y=2x-4。其他斜率情形切出的面积不能达到 12，因此所求直线唯一。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, the rectangle $OABC$ has two adjacent sides on the coordinate axes, with vertex $B(6, 4)$. A line passing through point $P(4, m)$ on side $BC$ bisects the area of the rectangle. What is the equation of this line?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} 

Since the adjacent sides of rectangle OABC are on the coordinate axes, and the vertex B is at (6, 4),\\
therefore, the intersection point of the diagonal lines of the rectangle is at (3, 2),\\
since point P(4, m) is a point on side BC,\\
therefore, P(4, 4),\\
since a line passing through the intersection point of the diagonal lines bisects the rectangle,\\
therefore, let the line passing through P(4, m) and bisecting the rectangle be $y=kx+b$,\\
substituting points (4, 4) and (3, 2) yields $\begin{cases}4k+b=4\\ 3k+b=2\end{cases}$,\\
solving, we get $\begin{cases}k=2\\ b=-4\end{cases}$,\\
therefore, the equation of this line is $y=2x-4$.\\
Hence, the answer is: $\boxed{y=2x-4}$
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: The figure is a rectangular coordinate system, O is at the origin, OA is along the positive direction of the x-axis, OC is along the positive direction of the y-axis, and OABC forms a rectangle; A is the lower-right vertex, C is the upper-left vertex, and B is the upper-right vertex. Point P is marked on the upper side BC, and BC is a horizontal side.

Reasoning: From the meaning of the problem, B(6,4), and the rectangular range is 0≤x≤6, 0≤y≤4, so the intersection point of the diagonals of the rectangle, namely the center, is ((0+6)/2,(0+4)/2)=(3,2). Point P(4,m) is on the upper side BC, and from the figure it can be seen that BC is the horizontal side y=4, so m=4, P=(4,4). Using the central symmetry of the rectangle, a straight line passing through the center of the rectangle bisects the area of the rectangle; therefore the required area-bisecting line passing through P should pass through the center (3,2). The slope through (4,4) and (3,2) is k=(4-2)/(4-3)=2. Substitute into the point-slope form: y-4=2(x-4), and simplifying gives y=2x-4.
